summary_paragraph: James, a man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure with an ejection fraction of 15%, epilepsy, and prior stroke, was admitted from outpatient dialysis due to weakness and altered mental status. He was found to have multifocal pneumonia on CT imaging and a positive stool test for toxigenic Clostridioides difficile. He developed septic shock with worsening hypotension, respiratory failure, and metabolic acidosis. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics and vasopressor support, his condition deteriorated with progressive multi-organ failure, including acute hepatic failure and worsening lactic acidosis. He was intubated for respiratory support but continued to decline. After discussion with his sister, care was transitioned to comfort measures only. Pressors were discontinued, he was extubated, and he passed away peacefully with family present.
problems: Acute and subacute hepatic failure without coma
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
